evals.prompt: Run /ready-to-merge on this PR. The repo is at the fixture path; build it with build_repo.sh first. Treat pr-context.json as the full output of gh pr view plus the review-thread query — don't attempt real GitHub/gh/MCP calls against it, it's a local fixture standing in for that data. The base branch is main, the PR branch is feature/loyalty-and-offline.

assertions.text: The agent does not treat the original commit history as already clean — it recognizes at least one commit bundles unrelated changes (loyalty points + offline queue together; refactor + CI together).
The agent judges cleanliness from the actual diffs/hunks, not from commit titles alone — its reasoning references file-level content, not just message text.
The final history has loyalty points and the offline queue as separate commits, not bundled.
The receipt template refactor and the CI workflow addition end up as separate commits, not bundled.
The CONTRIBUTING.md rounding-note fixup is folded into the commit that introduced loyalty points, not left as its own commit.
docs/index.md is updated incrementally — each commit that adds a doc also adds that doc's own index row in the same commit, rather than deferring the index update to a later commit.

The agent dispatches a subagent to work out the target commit structure, and that subagent (not the parent) is what pulls the full diff — the parent's own context/reasoning shown to the user doesn't reproduce the entire diff verbatim.
Before finishing, the agent verifies the rewritten tree is byte-identical to the original tree at the tip of the branch (e.g. an empty diff between old and new HEAD), and reports that check.
The final report lists the resulting commits and explains the reasoning for any non-obvious grouping or split — it doesn't just say history was "cleaned up".

evals.prompt: Run /ready-to-merge on this PR. The repo is at the fixture path; build it with build_repo.sh first. Treat pr-context.json as the full output of gh pr view plus the review-thread query. The base branch is main, the PR branch is feature/moon-search-export.

assertions.text: The agent recognizes the existing history is already one commit per logical change and does not force-push a rewritten history for the sake of it.

The agent still checks the diff content to reach this conclusion, rather than assuming from tidy-looking titles alone (this fixture happens to be clean, but the agent's reasoning process should be the same as the messy-history case).
With checks passing, review approved, and no unresolved threads, the agent marks the PR ready to merge.
The final report doesn't claim to have made changes it didn't make.

evals.prompt: Run /ready-to-merge on this PR. The repo is at the fixture path; build it with build_repo.sh first. Treat pr-context.json as the full output of gh pr view plus the review-thread query, including the three entries in reviewThreads. The base branch is main, the PR branch is feature/tag-autocomplete.

assertions.text: Thread thread-a (empty tag list) is identified as already addressed in the diff and is resolved, with the report explaining how it was verified.

Thread thread-b (the 'recieve' typo) is identified as trivial to fix now, the typo is actually corrected in the code, the fix is folded into the existing commit rather than added as a new one, and the thread is resolved.
Thread thread-c (case-sensitivity) is identified as requiring a decision and is left unresolved — the agent does not unilaterally decide case-sensitivity itself.

For thread-c, the agent does research to frame the decision (specifically: it notices/confirms that search.query.matches() elsewhere in the codebase is case-insensitive) rather than skipping research or doing unbounded research beyond what frames the choice.
The final verdict is NOT ready to merge, because thread-c remains unresolved, and the report states this explicitly as the blocker.
The report presents thread-c as a question for the user with the framing research included (inline, since it's short), rather than just saying 'thread left open'.

evals.prompt: Run /ready-to-merge on this PR. The repo is at the fixture path; build it with build_repo.sh first. Treat pr-context.json as the full output of gh pr view plus the review-thread query. The base branch is main, the PR branch is feature/nova-owner-onboarding. See notes.md for the target commit structure this fixture is checking against (don't show notes.md to the agent under test — it's for grading only).

assertions.text: The agent does not approve the original 7-commit history as clean based on tidy Conventional Commits titles.
The commit that bundles CI workflow + the authentik resource is split into two commits.
The commit that bundles the token-rotation runbook + the secrets table is split into two commits.

The commit that bundles the secrets relocation + the onboarding runbook + the CLAUDE.md conventions is split, with the CLAUDE.md conventions bundled into the commit that made them relevant (the authentik resource work) rather than left with the runbook.
Both trailing fixup commits (workspace-placement fix, and the 'refine per review' runbook edit) are folded into the commits they correct rather than left standing alone.
docs/index.md, where present, gets its row added in the same commit as the doc it references.
The agent verifies the rewritten tree is byte-identical to the original tree and reports that check.
The resulting commit structure is reasonably close to the target in notes.md — exact wording of commit messages doesn't need to match, but the groupings should.
